title: Provisional capacity escrow, invoice reconciliation, and operator runbook for burst usage
creator: Maya Ortiz
description: Customers using Dedicated capacity and temporary boost/surge features have reported unclear invoice line-items and occasional double charges when burst capacity is reconciled against reserved commits. Current behaviour: burst usage is billed as immediate overage at per-token rates and also counted against post-facto reserved amortization, causing confusion and disputes. This ticket proposes a 'provisional capacity escrow' model: meter burst/temporary boost consumption into a provisional ledger that is visible in Console and via API, hold it in an escrow state for a configurable reconciliation window (default 72 hours), and reconcile against reserved capacity or charge as overage at window close. Operator runbook and UI/alerting improvements required to support reconciliation exceptions, manual adjustments, and customer-facing invoice visibility.
acceptance_criteria: Burst consumption is recorded to a provisional escrow ledger separate from immediate invoiceable charges
Console surfaces provisional escrow usage per-tenant with timestamps, associated surge-pool id, and reconciliation ETA
Billing pipeline supports a reconciliation window configuration and attempts automatic match against committed capacity before final invoice generation
If reconciliation succeeds, provisional charges are credited/removed before invoice; if not, provisional usage becomes invoiceable with clear line-item explanations
Operators can view and apply manual adjustments (credits/refunds) through an internal UI; actions trigger audit log entries and customer notifications
API includes a allow_provisional flag for programmatic campaigns and webhooks for near-reconciliation alerts
End-to-end tests validate no double-billing occurs when reconciliation path is exercised under normal and failure modes
Metrics and dashboards for provisional ledger size, reconciliation lag, and reconciliation failure rate are present and alert when thresholds are breached
tasks: Design data model for provisional escrow ledger (ledger row, tenant_id, surge_pool_id, tokens, created_at, reconciliation_deadline, status, reconciled_against_commit_id)
Implement ingress path: tag burst allocations with provisional=true and write to escrow ledger instead of immediate overage invoice event
Extend billing pipeline: add reconciliation job that runs at reconciliation_deadline and attempts to match provisional rows to reserved capacity consumption or generates invoiceable events
Console work: provisional usage panel, expand cost breakdown to include escrowed items and expected reconciliation ETA
API/webhook: add provisional usage endpoint and webhook event types for reconciliation_succeeded/reconciliation_failed/near_deadline
Operator UI: small internal tool for searching escrow rows, applying credits, and recording adjustments with audit log
Add unit/integration tests and a staging migration script to backfill provisional status for recent burst events
Create Grafana dashboards and set SLO-based alerts for reconciliation failure rate > 0.5% over 1h and escrow ledger growth > 10% of daily committed capacity
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: reconciliation job fails leading to stuck escrow rows and delayed invoices; Mitigation: implement dead-letter queue and operator alert with manual reconciliation pathways

Risk: customers see inconsistent usage totals between realtime metrics and invoice preview; Mitigation: clearly label provisional values and default to showing both committed-consumed and provisional totals with explainer tooltip
Risk: operator errors when applying manual credits; Mitigation: require two-person review for credits above threshold and record immutable audit entries
Risk: increased billing pipeline complexity causing latency; Mitigation: reconciliation runs asynchronously and does not block realtime token accounting paths
notes: Proposal builds on previous surge-pool work but intentionally avoids changing surge allocation algorithms
Target reconciliation window default is 72 hours but must be configurable per-tenant and per-contract in Dedicated plans
Legal/billing team prefers a model where provisional charges are visible but not invoiceable until reconciliation cutoff
This feature needs coordination with Console, Billing, and Customer Success for rollout communication
